                      UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                           
7                                                                            
                    WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON                           
8                             AT SEATTLE                                     
9                                       CASE NO. C21-0563-JCC                
     IN RE VALVE ANTITRUST LITIGATION                                        
10                                                                            
                                        ORDER                                
11                                                                            
12                                                                            
13                                                                            
14                                                                            

15       This matter comes before the Court on proposed Intervenors Jason Brooks, Robert Austin 
16  McCuistion, and Apeirogon Games’ motions to intervene (Dkt. Nos. 208, 212). Having 
17  thoroughly considered the briefing and the relevant record, the Court hereby GRANTS the 
18  motions for the reasons explained herein.                                 
19       Plaintiffs Wolfire Games, LLC, Dark Catt Studios Holdings, Inc., and Dark Catt Studios 
20  Interactive, LLC recently moved the Court to certify a class of game developers and/or game 
21  publishers who paid Defendant for the use or sale of their games on Defendant’s game platform. 
22  (See Dkt. No. 181.) In doing so, Plaintiffs filed under seal unredacted versions of their motion 
23  and supporting exhibits, (see Dkt. Nos. 181, 182), in accordance with a prior order from this 
24  Court. (See Dkt. No. 178 at 5.) Defendant then moved to maintain the unredacted filings under 
25  seal, based on what it deems to be confidential information included in those filings. (See Dkt. 
26  No. 198.) That motion will be disposed of through a separate order. This order addresses the 
1  proposed Intervenors’ request for leave to intervene in this matter, which they bring solely for 
2  purposes of opposing Defendant’s motion to seal. (See Dkt. Nos. 208, 212.)  
3       Indeed, a person not directly involved in a legal proceeding but whose interest may be 
4  impacted by that proceeding may have the opportunity to intervene, either as a matter of right or 
5  upon court approval. Fed. R. Civ. P. 24. Most salient in this context, “[n]onparties seeking access 
6  to a judicial record in a civil case may do so by seeking permissive intervention under Rule 
7  24(b)(2).” San Jose Mercury News, Inc. v. U.S. Dist. Ct.—N. Dist. (San Jose), 187 F.3d 1096, 
8  1100 (9th Cir. 1999).                                                     
9       Proposed Intervenors Brooks and McCuistion, as gamers and consumers of Defendant’s 
10  platform, assert an interest in this matter and, correspondingly, the redacted information and 
11  sealed documents relating to Plaintiff’s motion for class certification. (See Dkt. No. 208 at 1–2.) 
12  Specifically, they contend that, as game consumers, they have effectively borne the cost of the 
13  allegedly inflated commissions paid to Defendant. (Id.) And because this Court has previously 
14  ruled that their claims must be brought through arbitration, they require access to this 
15  information to assist in pursuing their individual claims. (Id.) In addition, proposed Intervenor 
16  Apeirogon Games, as a game developer, asserts that it is an absent member of the proposed class 
17  and requires access to this information in order to assess whether to pursue claims individually, 
18  or as a member of the putative class. (See Dkt. No. 212 at 1–2.) The parties fail to challenge 
19  these contentions through briefs in opposition to the intervention motions. See LCR 7(b)(2). 
20  Therefore, the Court finds that proposed Intervenors do possess the requisite interest in the 
21  information at issue.                                                     
22       Thus, the only issue1 before the Court is timeliness. In making this assessment, the Court 

23                                                                            
        1 Typically, “[p]ermissive intervention . . . requires (1) an independent ground for 
24  jurisdiction; (2) a timely motion; and (3) a common question of law and fact between the 
   movant’s claim or defense and the main action.” Beckman Indus., Inc. v. Int’l Ins. Co., 966 F.2d 
25  470, 473 (9th Cir. 1992). However, a non-party aiming to intervene solely to request the 
   unsealing of a court record is not required to prove separate jurisdiction nor a common question. 
26                                                                            
   See Cosgrove v. Nat’l Fire & Marine Ins. Co., 770 F. App’x 793, 795 (9th Cir. 2019).  
1  considers three factors: “(1) the stage of the proceeding at which an applicant seeks to intervene; 
2  (2) the prejudice to other parties; and (3) the reason for and length of the delay.” League of 
3  United Latin Am. Citizens v. Wilson, 131 F.3d 1297, 1302 (9th Cir. 1997). “In exercising its 
4  discretion, the court must consider whether the intervention will unduly delay or prejudice the 
5  adjudication of the original parties’ rights.” Fed. R. Civ. P. 24(b)(3). And the absence of 
6  prejudice supports the determination that the motion is timely. See, e.g., Blum v. Merrill Lynch 
7  Pierce Fenner & Smith Inc., 712 F.3d 1349, 1354 (9th Cir. 2013).          
8       Here, proposed Intervenors sought leave to intervene and submitted opposition briefs in 
9  lockstep with the parties’ briefing on Defendant’s motion to seal. Therefore, there can be no 
10  prejudice to a party from the motions to intervene. And for that reason, the Court sees no basis to 
11  deny Movants’ requests.                                                   
12       Accordingly, the motions to intervene (Dkt. Nos. 208, 212) are GRANTED.  
13                                                                            
14       DATED this 19th day of April 2024.                                   
                                      A                                      
15                                                                            
16                                                                            
17                                                                            
                                      John C. Coughenour                     
18                                     UNITED STATES DISTRICT JUDGE
